parsed.summary: The file formalises R_k(3) as the least n such that every k-colouring of the edges of K_n has a monochromatic triangle. It states four results: R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞; an explicit lower bound (c·k^{1/3}/log k)^k with c = 1/(6e^38), conjoined with the same limit; log R_k ≥ (1/4−ε)k log k and ≤ (1+ε)k log k eventually; and log R_k = Θ(k log k). The main caveat is that the lower-coefficient theorem uses 1/4, although the paper's bound gives 1/3−o(1), so the name 'sharp_coefficients' is misleading.

glossary.plain: A k-colouring C of the edges of K_n has no monochromatic triangle: every colour class graph is 3-clique-free.
Every k-colouring of E(K_n) contains a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.note: For k = 0 and n ≥ 2 there are no colourings, so the property holds vacuously. This is irrelevant to the asymptotics.

glossary.plain: R_k(3) = the least n such that every k-colouring of K_n has a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.standard_concept: multicolour Ramsey number R(3,…,3) with k colours
glossary.note: sInf of a set of ℕ. The set is nonempty for k ≥ 1 by the finite Ramsey theorem, so there is no junk 0.

lean_claims.plain: For every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large k, (1/4−ε)·k·log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε)·k·log k.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) as k → ∞, i.e. R_k(3) = k^{Θ(k)}.

paper_claims.plain: There is an absolute constant c > 0 such that R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for every k ≥ 2.

coverage.why: The Lean statement fixes an explicit constant c = 1/(6e^38) in place of an unspecified absolute c. The excerpt does not state a value for c. The bound is correct in form and implies the existential statement.
The limit of R_k^{1/k} to ∞ is stated with Real.rpow over atTop on both sides.
The upper coefficient 1 matches. The lower coefficient is 1/4 instead of 1/3, which is weaker than the paper's 1/3−o(1).
This is log R_k = Θ(k log k) with the filter atTop on ℕ.

flags.explanation: The Lean statement hard-codes c = 1/(6e^38), whereas the paper's excerpt only asserts the existence of some absolute c. The constant is not in the excerpt, so it cannot be checked against the paper. As a theorem it is at least as strong as the existential claim, and it covers every k ≥ 2 as in the paper. The hypotheses are no stronger.
flags.probe_idea: Check against the full paper whether the proof yields exactly c = 1/(6e^38). Separately, confirm that the statement implies ∃ c > 0, ∀ k ≥ 2, (c·k^{1/3}/log k)^k ≤ R_k.

flags.explanation: The paper's lower bound gives log R_k ≥ (1/3−o(1)) k log k, but Lean only states the coefficient 1/4. The name 'sharp_coefficients' suggests sharpness that is not delivered, since the lower side is weaker than the paper's claim. The upper coefficient 1+ε matches the paper. For ε ≥ 1/4 the lower conjunct is trivial.
flags.probe_idea: State and prove the lower side with 1/3 in place of 1/4, i.e. ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ k in atTop, (1/3−ε)·k·log k ≤ log R_k. Alternatively, derive it from erdos_problem_183_explicit.
